# Results — Study 872 (Nominal-Price Illusion)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Kumar
(2009) & Birru-Wang (2016): the **nominal share price** ($10 vs $500) is a pure
money-illusion characteristic; retail lottery demand clusters in low-priced names, so cheap
names should carry the lottery look (higher vol / right skew) and **lower risk-adjusted
returns**. A book long the cheap / short the dear names should therefore earn a **negative**
`lo − hi` spread. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **nominal price level** (the adjusted Close), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by price; **long the cheapest 30%**, **short the priciest 30%**, equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book; report `lo − hi` (cheap − dear) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day; the short (dear) book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled cheap-vs-dear books; per-book annualised vol / skew / Sharpe; a 1,000-permutation two-sided placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship + proxy — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership**
set of liquid mega-caps. Two things blunt this signal by construction, and both lower power:
(1) **mega-caps are rarely cheap** — the price cross-section at the as-of date runs from
**~$20 (T)** to **~$1,063 (CAT)**, with *no single-digit* names, so the true retail-lottery
segment (penny / low-dollar stocks) is simply **absent** from the panel; (2) the cache is
`auto_adjust=True`, so `Close` is **split/dividend-back-adjusted** — an honest *proxy* for the
nominal trading price that is exact only near the as-of date and drifts below it into the past
(a name that later split shows a divided-down history). A pure-nominal replication needs raw
unadjusted closes, which the total-return cache does not preserve. **Honest low power** is the
headline caveat.

## The headline — long-cheap / short-dear spread (`lo − hi`)

Daily equal-weight cheapest-30% minus priciest-30% price-level spread (n = **4,146** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (cheap − dear)** | **+2.92 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+3.01** |
| one-sample *t* | +2.83 |
| cheap book / dear book | +8.75 bps / +5.82 bps (Welch *t* = +1.14) |

The claim **fails to replicate — and inverts.** Kumar / Birru-Wang predict cheap names
*under*-earn (a *negative* `lo − hi`); on this mega-cap universe the spread is **significantly
positive** (+2.92 bps/day, NW *t* = +3.01): the low-priced names actually **out-earned** the
expensive ones over 2010–2026. Within a mega-cap survivor set, the lower-dollar names (T, PFE,
BAC, KO, …) are the more value-tilted, cyclically-recovering names — the opposite of an
over-priced lottery. A significant **wrong-sign** result versus the claim ⇒ **Signal: None**.

## The risk-adjusted lottery read — more risk for less reward?

The over-priced-lottery hypothesis is really about *risk-adjusted* underperformance. It fails
on both legs here:

| book | ann. vol | return skew | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| cheap (bottom 30%) | 19.2% | −0.26 | **+1.15** |
| dear (top 30%) | 17.8% | −0.44 | +0.82 |

Cheap names carried only *slightly* more volatility (19.2% vs 17.8%) and a *less* negative
skew (−0.26 vs −0.44, i.e. a mildly more lottery-like tail — the one place the characteristic
weakly shows) — but their **Sharpe was higher, not lower** (+1.15 vs +0.82). The claim's core
prediction (lower risk-adjusted return for the cheap-looking names) is contradicted.

## Placebo — is the (reversed) relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the price sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted** panel
(signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50), two-sided:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+2.92 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.019 bps (1.218) |
| position of observed | ≈ **2.4σ into the right tail** (two-sided p = **0.014**) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed +2.92 bps sits well into the **right** tail,
so the (opposite-sign) relation is real and not a lucky sort — the sign is simply the reverse
of the literature's on this universe.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=2,012) | +2.66 bps | **+2.11** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +3.18 bps | **+2.16** |

The (wrong-sign) out-performance of cheap names holds in **both** halves — this is a robust
sign-reversal, not one era's artefact. That robustness is exactly what makes it a clean
**None** rather than noise.

## The timer — can you get paid for it (even the reversed book)?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short (dear) pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +2.92 bps | 2.14 bps | **+0.79 bps** | +0.76 | 0.19 | +2.0%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +2.92 bps | 10.14 bps | **−7.21 bps** | −6.98 | −1.72 | −18.2%/yr |

Even the *data-mined sign-flip* — long cheap / short dear, which earns +2.92 bps/day gross —
does **not** survive friction: at 1 bp one-way the net is +0.79 bps/day but *insignificant*
(*t* = +0.76), and at any realistic cost (5 bps) it is firmly negative. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel where each name's latent "cheapness" fixes its price level, inflates
its vol and right-skew (the lottery look, always on), and — with `edge>0` — depresses its
forward mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* | lottery look (cheap vs dear) |
|---|--:|---|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.15** (sd 0.92), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** | — |
| planted (`edge = 0.0016`, seed 872) | **−3.69** (Welch *t* = −4.01) | vol 19.8% vs 6.3%, skew +0.89 vs +0.33 |

The detector recovers a *planted* Kumar/Birru-Wang **under-earn** relation cleanly (correctly
*negative*), plants the lottery look (cheap names visibly more volatile & right-skewed), and
never fires on the null — so the **positive** real-tape result is a genuine sign-reversal on
the mega-cap universe, not a bug. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The nominal-price money-illusion premium does **not** replicate on 50
  liquid US mega-caps. The specified long-cheap / short-dear spread is **+2.92 bps/day**
  (NW *t* = **+3.01**) — significant but *opposite in sign* to the claim (cheap names
  **out**-earned, and with a *higher* Sharpe, +1.15 vs +0.82), holding in both eras
  (*t* = +2.11 / +2.16), ≈2.4σ into the right tail of a 1,000-permutation placebo, with a clean
  20-seed synthetic control. The retail-lottery segment (penny / low-dollar stocks) is *absent*
  from a mega-cap survivor panel — honest low power — and where the price illusion should bite,
  the mega-cap cross-section instead rewards its lower-dollar (value-tilted) names.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even the data-mined sign-flip book is a mirage: net +0.79 bps/day
  at 1 bp one-way but *insignificant* (*t* = +0.76), and −7.21 bps/day at 5 bps. No version of
  the book survives realistic friction.
